findings.text: the landing comment cites 'Commit 109c92af adds docs/evidence/data/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet/login-slice-window-start.json', and that sha is not on the branch: it is the pre-amend revision of 1ba6d75f (reflog in the node's own worktree reads 109c92af HEAD@{2} commit, then 1ba6d75f HEAD@{1} commit (amend); git diff 109c92af 1ba6d75f --stat prints nothing, so the tree -- and the cited artifact -- is identical and the message is all that changed). There is no fabrication and no wrong content; what fails is resolvability, which is the half that matters for a citation a later reader is meant to open: from the merged branch 109c92af resolves to no object. Cite 1ba6d75f, or drop the sha and link the archive anchor, which is stable.

justifications.durability: the sample and its landing record are separate commits, the record names both, and the gate log's first line names the revision it ran at (86e8ab34) and the tree. The environment-independent part is weaker: the landing comment in the plan cites commit 109c92af, which is the pre-amend revision of 1ba6d75f and is not an ancestor of any ref a reader of the merged branch will hold, so the citation resolves for nobody after the merge.
justifications.fit: the committed payload is data with no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in it; the figure file name states what it plots; the two commit subjects are conventional and both carry bodies; the accession vocabulary in the file is the instrument's own field names. The only naming drift is between the amended subject ('opens the drain window') and the committed documents ('attrition window'), two words for the same step that the plan itself uses interchangeably.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's goal is to commit the login slice throttling sample that opens the seventh step's attrition window, and commit 1ba6d75f adds exactly one file, docs/evidence/data/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet/login-slice-window-start.json: the sampler's payload for user.slice/user-39486.slice on the login node, whose values match the plan's step-one and step-seven semantics (host, boot, quota, period counters, permitted and cumulative share). The landing record states the reading is the window's start point and not a result, which is the semantics step seven needs.
justifications.scope_discipline: the node's two commits are 1ba6d75f, which touches only docs/evidence/data/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet/login-slice-window-start.json, and 86e8ab34, which touches only docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html, docs/figures/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet/window-start-cumulative-reading.svg and docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html -- all four inside the declared write paths and nothing else. numstat shows 72/41/7 added and 0 removed, so the documentation commit is append-only. The library module the sample comes from, imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, appears in neither commit, and no test file is among the write paths, so the declared negative-control exemption is correct.

JUSTIFICATION evidence: the two relations the fence names hold exactly, re-derived from the committed file with json.load: throttled_share 0.3690189573067196 == throttled_usec 5795334085321 / permitted_usec 15704705600000 (bit-exact float equality, absolute difference 0.0), and permitted_usec == nr_periods 39261764 x the 400000 quota == 15704705600000 (exact). The file alone, without the manifest, carries everything an interval share against a later reading on the same boot needs: boot_id and uptime_seconds establish the same boot and an order, cpu_max carries the quota, and all three period counters plus usage_usec are present, so a later reading yields delta(throttled_usec)/delta(permitted_usec) with delta(permitted_usec) = delta(nr_periods) x 400000. Demonstrated rather than argued: from a compute node I read the same slice over ssh twice, got the same boot_id 82c41dfa-a445-4fb2-8416-04b44c3d874c, and computed interval shares of 1.276 over the 2472.7 s from the committed reading (12624429662/9890800000) and 0.828 over the following 343.3 s (1136382398/1373200000). Corroboration of the verbatim claim from a source I did not produce: the run's own stream.jsonl line 1043 carries the ssh stdout of the committing read at 16:23:01Z, and its JSON block is byte-identical to the committed file (473 bytes, sha256 15f8e788c02369db; the file's od tail '6 \n   } \n } \n' matches the trailing bytes the worker dumped from the same stdout). The file's mtime 18:23 CEST equals 16:23Z. Caveat, already documented by the plan and therefore not a defect here: the ratio is unclamped and can exceed one, so the interval form is a draw rather than a level.
